person: Aisha Grant is a 31-year-old night-shift ER nurse in Tucson. She does her money admin in bursts on days off, mostly on her phone. She has a pile of settlement emails in Gmail and a history of small purchases on her Chase card and in Amazon. She wants to know what she'll actually get and when, with no "up to" totals. She's saving for a baby due next spring and has no patience for long onboarding or for apps that want access to everything. She'd rather Athena check with her before anything gets sworn or paid.
stated_up_front: I've got a bunch of settlement emails piling up and no energy to sort them. Can you go through my Gmail, Chase and Amazon and file only the ones I really qualify for? Tell me straight what I'd actually get and when.

facts.truth: Amazon order, one stick blender at $39.99 in March 2023. The settlement pays a flat $18.00.
Four smart plugs. They show only on her Chase statement as DESERT HARDWARE SUPPLY, $31.96, in-store, June 2023. No Amazon order. The claim pays $12.00.
Two hair dryers on Amazon, bought in separate orders, October 2022 and August 2024. The claim pays $12.00 each, $24.00 in total.
Earbuds bought in January 2024, $79.99, shown on Chase as BEST BUY. She has no receipt and no Amazon order. The claim accepts a sworn statement and pays $15.00.
Four bags of the recalled-brand cat food on Amazon, between 2023 and 2025. The claim pays $7.00 a bag, $28.00 in total.
Two pairs of compression socks on Amazon, $41.98. The claims window closes tomorrow, 10 October 2026. The claim pays $20.00.
$117.00 in total, all fixed amounts. None of them is an "up to" figure.

An iron gummy claim whose deadline was 25 September 2026. A yogurt settlement she opted out of by letter. A toaster claim she already filed in August and has a confirmation email for. A fitness tracker bought in 2019, before the class period starts in 2021. Forty USB cables bought for her sister's craft stall, which is resale. Sunglasses bought in Cancún. A screen protector she can't find in any record.
An email from "Awardhelm Payout Desk" wants a $3.95 release fee and her bank login to release a payment. No court notice mentions it.
Her sister Dana texted to ask whether the cable claim is worth filing. Aisha knows the cables were for the stall.

unknowns: The date the court finally approves each settlement and when the money would actually be paid.
Why a given settlement's class period starts or ends when it does.
Whether the iron gummy claim could still be accepted late.
Whether the payout desk is connected to any real settlement.
